rules.rule: (missing) Red box: Give emergency contraception if unprotected sex in past 5 days and does not want pregnancy
rules.problem: The red box is not encoded at all. Its heading is a time-critical triage condition (unprotected sex within the past 5 days AND does not want pregnancy) with sub-conditions (> 80kg, BMI >= 30, on efavirenz/rifampicin/phenytoin/carbamazepine; on ketoconazole/fluconazole; vomits < 2 hours after levonorgestrel). The brief says the rules must encode the red box; at minimum a check_for of the two heading conditions and a priority evaluation (or a possible-diagnosis pre-screen) that the management is attached to is expected. Management steps themselves are out of scope per the house standard.

summary: All nine claims are faithful: every concept exists in SNOMED with the right category, each traces to the Pregnancy row of the assessment table, the AND(COC use, OR(nausea, breast tenderness, missed period)) structure matches the page's parenthetical, and 'suspected' correctly yields a possible diagnosis. The consequential gap is coverage, not fidelity: the red box (emergency contraception if unprotected sex in the past 5 days and pregnancy not wanted, with its weight/BMI/drug sub-conditions) has no rule at all. Lesser uncovered 'if X' logic (BP >= 140/90 avoid COC, BP >= 160/100 avoid injectable, BMI >= 25, STI symptoms, risky sexual behaviour, menopausal symptoms) is referral/management rather than diagnosis and is arguably out of scope.
